title: IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), 2023 update
content: International Olympic Committee consensus statement, British Journal of Sports Medicine 2023 — Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs) results from prolonged low energy availability (energy intake insufficient to cover the energy cost of exercise plus normal body functions), and can impair multiple body systems: bone health, menstrual/hormonal function, immune function, cardiovascular health, psychological health, and growth/development — affecting both men and women, not only female athletes as earlier framing (the 'Female Athlete Triad') suggested.

title: IOC consensus statement on Relative Energy Deficiency in Sport (REDs), 2023 update
content: IOC REDs 2023 — Screening/warning signs include unexplained performance decline, menstrual cycle disruption, frequent illness/injury, and persistently very low reported energy intake relative to training load. Product implication: this codebase's safety-triage layer must treat sustained very-low-calorie targets combined with high training volume as a REDs-risk signal requiring EARLY_REVIEW/support-and-refer handling — never continuing to push a more aggressive deficit or higher training volume once these signals are present — consistent with this app's existing 'never continue toward more aggressive cuts under a safety flag' rule.
